explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/946: are there infinitely many n with τ(n) = τ(n+1)? Answered yes by Heath-Brown [He84]. The statement is {n | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n+1)}.Infinite, with σ 0 the divisor-counting function; n = 0 is not a spurious solution (σ 0 0 = 0 ≠ 1). Faithful (the source phrases it as a question, now answered yes, so the unnegated form is correct).
